scope: Hugging Face NFL / American-football dataset candidates, metadata-only review
method: Hugging Face dataset cards, Hub API metadata, and publicly published previews/README content only. No dataset files were downloaded, opened, or committed.
non_goals_observed: no data added to production artifacts
Hugging Face metadata not treated as sufficient provenance
no paid/gated dataset treated as usable without explicit license/access review
approval_statement: No dataset reviewed in this audit is approved for production use or governed experimental use. Zero datasets classified external_candidate. Any follow-up must be a separate, narrowly scoped issue.
cross_cutting_findings: Four of the six tabular/QA candidate lanes (4th-downs, WR 2025, both Karmane datasets) are downstream repackagings of nflverse data. TIBER-Data already integrates nflverse first-hand via nflreadpy (see data/processed/evidence/*.source_backed.json). Mirroring a third-party repackaging would insert an unverifiable middleman between TIBER and a source it already holds under known terms.

Two candidates carry license-metadata conflicts: both Karmane datasets declare an MIT tag while enforcing a paid Gumroad purchase gate with manual approval; keremberke/nfl-object-detection has no Hub license tag while its card body claims Public Domain over what appears to be copyrighted NFL broadcast imagery.

The correct acquisition pattern for every tabular capability represented here (4th-down decisions, WR player-game features, rest/travel schedule context, usage/TD trends) is in-house derivation from the already-integrated nflreadpy/nflverse upstream, not external mirroring.

datasets.name: afzalmengal/nfl-4th-downs-dataset
datasets.license_detail: No Hub license tag; no license statement in README. No redistribution or mirroring right exists; fail closed.
datasets.source_lineage: Unstated by author. README says 'filtered from full NFL play-by-play data (1999-2025)'. Column vocabulary (game_id, posteam/defteam, yardline_100, epa, wp, def_wp, spread_line, total_line) is the exact nflfastR/nflverse play-by-play vocabulary, so this is almost certainly an unattributed nflverse derivative. Unverified.
datasets.schema_summary: Play-level 4th-down situations: game context (game_id, season, qtr, game_seconds_remaining), field position (yardline_100, ydstogo, goal_to_go), teams (posteam, defteam, home/away), score state, win probability (wp, def_wp), EPA, betting lines (spread_line, total_line), coaching names, team weekly/yearly performance features, and a decision label (go/punt/fg).
datasets.tiber_overlap: High at the source level: TIBER already integrates nflverse via nflreadpy. No committed TIBER artifact currently covers play-level 4th-down decisions, but the underlying rows are derivable in-house from the same upstream.
datasets.leakage_risk: epa/wp/def_wp are model-derived values and the label column is the realized decision; the card does not separate pregame from post-snap information. Team performance features have unverified as-of semantics (possible future-week contamination within a season). Unsafe near Forecast/validation without a full as-of audit.
datasets.identity_risk: Team-code and game_id keyed (no player grain). game_id convention presumed nflverse-style but unverified; coaching names are free text; season/week join semantics unverified.
datasets.classification_rationale: No license means no legal basis to mirror or redistribute; lineage is unattributed and unverifiable; the dataset was created two days before this audit by an unknown uploader; and every column is derivable in-house from TIBER's already-integrated nflverse upstream under known terms.
datasets.recommended_next_action: None for this dataset. If 4th-down decision analytics are ever wanted, open a separate issue to derive an in-house artifact from nflreadpy play-by-play with explicit as-of semantics.

datasets.name: SebastianAndreu/24679_NFL_WR_Dataset_2025
datasets.license_detail: MIT Hub tag and card statement; redistribution technically permitted. Card states not for real-money gambling or player contract decisions.

shape.seasons: 2025 (partial; created 2025-10-03, last modified 2025-10-30, i.e. an in-season snapshot)

datasets.source_lineage: Card cites nflverse/nflverse-data play-by-play; built by two processing pipelines (defense-adjusted metrics; quarter/WP-bucketed breakdowns). CMU course project (24-679: Designing and Deploying AI/ML Systems).
datasets.schema_summary: WR player-game rows: targets, receptions, yards, air yards, YAC, TDs, EPA/WPA, target share, air-yards share, WOPR, aDOT, catch rate, explosive-play rates, red-zone/end-zone/third-down splits, quarter and WP-bucket breakdowns, defense-adjusted deltas vs league average, QB context (CPOE etc.), weather/venue/surface, betting lines.
datasets.tiber_overlap: Direct: TIBER's source-backed 2025 evidence (player_weekly_usage_2025 6,326 rows; player_weekly_ppr_outcomes_2025 6,394 rows, weeks 1-22, all positions) already covers this grain from the same upstream, with broader position and week coverage than this 1,918-row WR-only in-season snapshot.
datasets.leakage_risk: High for any 2025 Forecast/validation use: rows are postgame outcomes; defense-adjusted and league-average features are computed over an unspecified window and may fold later-week information into earlier-week rows. Unverified as-of discipline throughout.
datasets.identity_risk: Player identification scheme unverified (names vs GSIS IDs); no demonstrated join path to tiber_identity_crosswalk_v1 (25 sleeper-only records); season/week key semantics unverified; WR-only filter creates silent-population duplicate-semantics risk vs TIBER's all-position artifacts.
datasets.classification_rationale: License is clean but the data is redundant with TIBER's own governed source path, single-season, mid-season snapshot, course-project provenance with undocumented derivation choices, and 6 total downloads. Its value is the feature vocabulary (WOPR, aDOT, WP-bucketed splits, defense-adjusted deltas), not the rows.
datasets.recommended_next_action: May be cited as a public schema/feature-vocabulary reference when designing future WR/role-usage contract fields. No mirror, no ingestion.

datasets.name: Karmane/nfl-rest-advantage-travel-spot-research
datasets.license_detail: Hub tag says MIT but access is manually gated behind a paid Gumroad purchase with username/email verification. Effective terms are the unpublished purchase terms, not MIT. Contradiction unresolved; fail closed per issue guardrail on paid/gated datasets.

shape.seasons: 27 seasons of completed games, latest source game 2026-02-08

datasets.source_lineage: Card cites nflverse game schedules and completed game records; team-side observations (one row per team per game).
datasets.schema_summary: 87 columns: schedule context (rest days, short-week flags, travel distance), market data (spread, moneyline, totals), environment, rolling team trend metrics, and postgame outcomes (scores, ATS results, over/under) with claimed pregame/postgame column separation. 618 playoff games, 2,418 rest-advantage games, 581 short-week scenarios.
datasets.tiber_overlap: Partial conceptual overlap with team-week lanes (team_week_raw_v0 contract, team pace/pass environment). No committed TIBER artifact covers rest/travel/schedule-spot context; underlying schedule data is derivable in-house from nflverse.
datasets.leakage_risk: Rows mix pregame features and postgame outcomes; the pregame/postgame separation is claimed but unverifiable without the paid data. Rolling trend windows have unverified as-of semantics.
datasets.identity_risk: Team-game grain; team code vocabulary and game key convention unverified against TIBER team identity; no player identity surface.
datasets.classification_rationale: Paid/gated access with contradictory license metadata fails the issue's guardrail outright. The public card and preview are legitimately useful as vocabulary for a future Teamstate schedule-context contract (rest days, travel, short-week spots), but the data itself must not be purchased, mirrored, or ingested under this audit.
datasets.recommended_next_action: May be cited (card/preview only) when scoping a future schedule/rest/travel context contract. Any data need should be met by in-house derivation from nflverse schedules.

datasets.name: Karmane/nfl-anytime-touchdown-parlay-usage-trends
datasets.license_detail: Same publisher and same pattern as the rest-advantage dataset: MIT Hub tag behind a paid Gumroad manual gate. Effective terms unpublished; fail closed.
datasets.source_lineage: Card cites public nflverse sources: snap counts, player identifiers, weekly player stats, schedules; states no proprietary touchdown-prop feeds used. One row per offensive skill player per completed game with logged snaps.
datasets.schema_summary: 126 columns: ~50 pregame (snaps, snap pct, rest context, moneyline/spread, implied team totals, rolling last-3/last-5 usage, opponent allowance rates), ~40 postgame outcomes (TDs, yardage, shares, threshold flags like cleared_anytime_td), ~36 metadata (player IDs/names, position, team, game IDs, weather, venue, timestamps).
datasets.tiber_overlap: Direct grain overlap with TIBER's player-weekly usage lane (player_weekly_usage_2025.source_backed.json) and FORGE weekly inputs, though those currently cover 2025 only vs this dataset's 2013-2024. All inputs cited are nflverse surfaces TIBER can pull first-hand.
datasets.leakage_risk: Rows mix pregame and postgame columns; separation is claimed but unverifiable without paid access. Rolling windows and opponent-allowance features have unverified as-of discipline. Betting/parlay framing invites target definitions (threshold flags) that TIBER does not govern.
datasets.identity_risk: Player IDs and names present but scheme unverified (likely nflverse GSIS if the lineage claim holds); join to tiber_identity_crosswalk_v1 unproven; multi-season player-team movement semantics unverified.
datasets.classification_rationale: Same paid-gate/license contradiction as its sibling; guardrail fails it for any data use. The pregame/postgame column discipline and rolling-usage feature shapes on the public card are legitimate design reference for future usage/TD feature work; the rows themselves are not usable and are in any case derivable in-house.
datasets.recommended_next_action: May be cited (card/preview only) as feature-shape reference. Multi-season usage/TD needs should be met by in-house nflreadpy ingestion under the existing multi-season coverage lane.

datasets.name: keremberke/nfl-object-detection
datasets.license_detail: No Hub license tag in API metadata. Card body (Roboflow export boilerplate) claims Public Domain. Underlying content is 9,947 frames of NFL game footage with helmet annotations; NFL broadcast/endzone imagery is copyrighted, so an unqualified Public Domain claim by a re-exporter is not credible without verification. Fail closed.
datasets.source_lineage: Exported from Roboflow 2022-12-29 via roboflow2huggingface. Original imagery source unstated; helmet-label taxonomy (helmet, helmet-blurred, helmet-difficult, helmet-partial, helmet-sideline) matches the NFL Health & Safety Kaggle helmet-detection competition family, whose data carries its own competition terms. Chain of custody unverifiable.
datasets.schema_summary: Object-detection images with five helmet-related bounding-box labels; no tabular schema, no player/team/game identity fields.
datasets.tiber_overlap: None. TIBER-Data has no image/vision surface and no consumer for tracking or visual football-state data.
datasets.leakage_risk: Not applicable to Forecast/player-history lanes (no tabular outcomes).
datasets.identity_risk: None at the schema level (no identity fields); residual risk is depicting identifiable players in copyrighted footage, which is a rights question rather than a join-key question.
datasets.classification_rationale: Provenance chain is unverifiable, the Public Domain claim conflicts with the probable copyright status of the underlying footage and with the absence of a Hub license tag, the dataset is stale (2022), and it has zero overlap with any current TIBER pipeline. The topic (visual football-state / player-safety research) could someday be a research lane, but this artifact must not be the vehicle; any future effort should re-source imagery under verified terms.

datasets.name: leomaurodesenv/QASports2
datasets.license_detail: MIT Hub tag, public. However, contexts are scraped from sports Fandom wikis, whose text is typically CC-BY-SA; an MIT relabel by the dataset author cannot strip the source text's attribution/share-alike obligations. Redistribution of the text is therefore encumbered regardless of the tag.

shape.rows: ~1.09M unique rows in the primary 'all' configuration
shape.row_count_note: The Hub-aggregate figure of 2,183,926 rows sums the 'all' configuration together with the overlapping per-sport configurations and therefore double-counts by roughly 2x. Use the 'all' configuration (~873k train / ~109k validation / ~109k test) to size any future benchmark-reference work.
shape.subsets: 21 per-sport subsets (including American Football) that overlap the 'all' configuration

datasets.source_lineage: Extractive QA built over sports wiki pages (Fandom); processing scripts published at github.com/leomaurodesenv/qasports-dataset-scripts.
datasets.schema_summary: qa_id, context_id, context_title, context_url, context_categories, context (passage), question, answer{text, offset}. Extractive QA grain.
datasets.tiber_overlap: None. TIBER-Data has no QA/eval artifact surface. No identity/production/roster overlap.
datasets.leakage_risk: Not applicable to Forecast/player-history lanes. For a future eval: wiki text embeds outcomes of historical events, so any benchmark built from it must treat contexts as containing realized results.
datasets.identity_risk: Player/team references are free text from wikis with no controlled IDs; unusable as an identity source; low risk because no join is proposed.
datasets.classification_rationale: Legitimate published QA resource relevant only to future TIBER-Bench / football-domain QA eval design (schema, split design, per-sport subsets). Not source material for Forecast/Data. Text mirroring is discouraged by the upstream wiki-license caveat; citation and design reference suffice.
datasets.recommended_next_action: May be cited in future TIBER-Bench eval design. No mirror.

datasets.name: PedroCJardim/QASports
datasets.license_detail: Same lineage family and same caveat as QASports2: MIT tag over wiki-scraped contexts.
datasets.source_lineage: Wiki pages of 3 sports (~54k documents); published at Brazilian Symposium on Databases 2023; full data also on OSF (osf.io/n7r23).
datasets.schema_summary: id_qa, context_id, context, question, answer{text, offset}, context_title, url. Extractive QA grain.
datasets.classification_rationale: Predecessor of QASports2 with a documented paper trail; if either is ever used as eval-design reference, prefer QASports2 as the current version and cite the paper. Not source material for Forecast/Data.

allowed_followups.description: If 4th-down decision analytics are wanted, open a separate issue to derive an in-house play-level artifact from nflreadpy play-by-play with explicit as-of semantics (not a mirror of any dataset above).

If schedule/rest/travel context is wanted for Teamstate, open a separate spec issue for a schedule-context contract, using the Karmane rest-advantage public card as vocabulary reference only, sourced in-house from nflverse schedules.
If a football-domain QA eval is wanted for TIBER-Bench, open a separate design issue citing QASports2 as reference; do not mirror wiki text.
